Answer: C
Reason: The chest X-rays demonstrate bilateral upper lobe peripheral opacities with apical predominance, a pattern of transient pulmonary infiltrates that is characteristic of Eosinophilic Granulomatosis with Polyangiitis (EGPA). This finding aligns with the classic radiographic presentation of EGPA, distinguishing it from other vasculitides or infections that typically present with lower lobe or central involvement.
